Common openings:
- "Hello,"
- "Hey Naomi,"
- "Hey Parker,"

Common core lines:
- ">"
- ">>>>"
- "Best,"

Common closings:
- "Best,"
- "We support any questions related to course and functionality, you’ll have to contact Matt directly for this kind of collaboration. We don’t have Matt’s email, you’ll have to reach out on his personal website or Twitter."

- "related to the course" — 8 (20.5%)

- Openings trend toward: "Hello,"
- Closings often include: "Best,"

generated_query: I’m a support coordinator for an online learning platform, and I just received an email from a journalist who wants to set up an interview with our lead instructor, Kent. We only handle questions about course content and technical issues—collaborations have to go through Kent personally. Could you draft a polite reply that thanks them for reaching out, explains our scope, and directs them to contact Kent via his personal website or Twitter instead?

edit_instructions.target_text: We support any questions related to course and functionality, you’ll have to contact Kent directly for this kind of collaboration. We don’t have Kent’s email, you’ll have to reach out on his personal website or Twitter.
edit_instructions.rationale: Removing the line instructing to contact Kent directly eliminates the key step needed by the user query.
